beats.narration: DeepSeek V3 has six hundred seventy-one billion parameters, but uses thirty-seven billion per token. How does it keep its experts balanced without a penalty?
beats.narration_text: DeepSeek-V3: (1) show me how a token picks 8 of 256 experts, (2) explain how it balances expert load without a big auxiliary loss, (3) tell me what multi-head latent attention saves in the KV cache — with numbers from config.json.

props.command: DeepSeek-V3: (1) show me how a token picks 8 of 256 experts, (2) explain how it balances expert load without a big auxiliary loss, (3) tell me what multi-head latent attention saves in the KV cache — with numbers from config.json.
output: ROUTE   sigmoid score → top-8 of 256 + 1 shared
BALANCE per-expert bias, nudged each step

beats.narration: One idea: balance the experts with a bias, not a penalty. The routing, the bias, the memory, and then the catch.
beats.narration_text: One idea: balance the experts with a bias, not a penalty. The routing, the bias, the memory, and then the catch.

props.title: DeepSeek-V3, Balanced Without a Penalty?
thesis: 671B parameters, 37B per token. A per-expert bias steers which experts
get picked — so balancing no longer leans on a big loss term.

roadmap.label: The routing
roadmap.body: 1 shared + 8 of 256 routed experts per token.

roadmap.label: The bias
roadmap.body: It picks the experts. It never weighs them.

roadmap.label: The catch
roadmap.body: A tiny balance loss stays; all 671B still sit in memory.

beats.narration: Three dense layers, then fifty-eight expert layers. Each token visits one shared expert, and eight of two hundred fifty-six routed ones. Thirty-seven billion, of six hundred seventy-one.
beats.narration_text: Three dense layers, then fifty-eight expert layers. Each token visits one shared expert, and eight of two hundred fifty-six routed ones. Thirty-seven billion, of six hundred seventy-one.

props.heading: Where the experts live

moves.label: EXPERTS
moves.detail: Layers 4–61: 1 shared + 8 of 256 routed experts, width 2,048.

moves.label: ATTENTION
moves.detail: Every layer: multi-head latent attention, 128 heads.

props.keepNote: 37B of 671B per token — but only if the router spreads tokens across all 256.

beats.narration: The trick: every expert gets a bias. It's added only when picking the top eight, never to the gate weights. After each step, overloaded experts get their bias lowered, idle ones raised. No loss term fights the real objective.
beats.narration_text: The trick: every expert gets a bias. It's added only when picking the top eight, never to the gate weights. After each step, overloaded experts get their bias lowered, idle ones raised. No loss term fights the real objective.

props.spark: The bias picks. It never weighs.
props.heading: Auxiliary-loss-free balancing

moves.label: SCORE
moves.detail: Sigmoid affinity of the token to each of 256 experts.

moves.label: PICK
moves.detail: Top-8 of score + bias: the bias decides who is picked.

moves.label: WEIGH
moves.detail: Gate weights come from the raw scores — no bias.

moves.label: NUDGE
moves.detail: End of each step: overloaded → bias − γ, idle → bias + γ.

props.keepNote: Balance is steered through selection, so no balance loss pulls against the language-modelling loss.

beats.narration: Now memory. Standard attention here would cache about forty-one thousand numbers per token, per layer. Latent attention caches five hundred seventy-six. Seventy-one times smaller.
beats.narration_text: Now memory. Standard attention here would cache about forty-one thousand numbers per token, per layer. Latent attention caches five hundred seventy-six. Seventy-one times smaller.

props.spark: Cache the latent, not the heads.
props.heading: KV cache per token, per layer
props.exception: 40,960 ÷ 576 ≈ 71x. Across 61 layers at BF16: 576 × 61 × 2 bytes ≈ 70 KB per token.
props.source: Computed from deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3 config.json (kv_lora_rank 512, qk_rope_head_dim 64) · arXiv:2412.19437 §2.1.1

beats.narration: Two caveats. A tiny balance loss stays on as a backstop, so it's mostly penalty-free, not completely. And all six hundred seventy-one billion weights still have to sit in memory.
beats.narration_text: Two caveats. A tiny balance loss stays on as a backstop, so it's mostly penalty-free, not completely. And all six hundred seventy-one billion weights still have to sit in memory.

props.heading: What the headline leaves out

moves.label: BACKSTOP
moves.detail: A sequence-wise balance loss stays on, with an extremely small weight.

moves.label: MEMORY
moves.detail: 37B active is compute per token; all 671B weights are still stored.

moves.label: MTP
moves.detail: It mainly densifies training; speculative decoding with it is optional.

props.keepNote: Auxiliary-loss-free is the main mechanism, not the whole story.

beats.narration: The verdict. The bias steers selection and leaves the gate weights clean. The memory win is real, and checkable from the config. But sparse compute is not sparse memory.

artifactLines: Routing: 1 shared + 8 of 256 experts → 37B of 671B per token.
Balance: a per-expert bias steers selection; gate weights are untouched.
Memory: MLA caches 576 values per token per layer — ~71x under MHA at these dims.
Caveat: mostly penalty-free, not completely; sparse compute is not sparse memory.
